citations.title: Agentic CAD According to Engineers Building It
excerpts: That last category is where we started with [AutoReview](https://www.colabsoftware.com/product/autoreview) . Checking a design against a team’s own standards and checklists is exactly the kind of bounded, verifiable work agents do well today, because an engineer confirms every finding before it matters.

We call it the “messy middle” as a shorthand. A general-purpose model doesn’t know why a previous program made a certain tradeoff, or which supplier is best for a specific part, or which issue caused a lot of rework last time. That specific failure is what our [Lessons Learned Agent](https://www.colabsoftware.com/product/ai-lessons-learned) addresses. It finds similar past designs and surfaces the decisions made on them during a new review, so the work starts from company context instead of internet averages.
Jeremy Andrews Jeremy Andrews CTO [linkedin](https://www.linkedin.com/in/jeremyandrewscolab/) Jeremy Andrews is CoLab’s CTO and Co-Founder.
He is a mechanical engineer who ran DFM reviews on Tesla Model 3 battery pack components and at General Dynamics before co-founding CoLab in 2017.

The second article discusses CoLab's bounded AutoReview approach and how its Lessons Learned Agent surfaces historical design context. Both are attributed to Jeremy Andrews, an engineer and CTO. The second article mixes technical explanation with broader industry discussion, making qualification somewhat interpretive.
